back: meth (1), eth (2), prop (3), but (4), pent (5), hex (6).
notes: Pent and hex are needed for ZIMSEC; Cambridge stops at four carbons.

front: Endings for alkanes, alkenes, alcohols and carboxylic acids
How do you number the chain when naming?
back: From the end nearer the functional group, so it gets the lower number (but-1-ene, not but-3-ene).

front: Is the carbon of –COOH counted in the name?
back: Yes: it is carbon 1 of the chain. $\ce{CH3COOH}$ is ethanoic acid (two carbons).
Propan-1-ol $\ce{CH3CH2CH2OH}$ (–OH on an end carbon); propan-2-ol $\ce{CH3CH(OH)CH3}$ (–OH on the middle carbon).

notes: Same molecular formula, C₄H₈. Supplement and ZIMSEC.

back: Alcohol part first, ending -yl; acid part second, ending -oate (e.g. ethyl ethanoate).
$\ce{CH3COOCH2CH3}$ (acid part written first in the formula).
notes: Made from ethanol and ethanoic acid. Supplement and ZIMSEC.

back: A $\ce{-CH3}$ branch on a carbon chain, as in methylpropane, $\ce{CH3CH(CH3)CH3}$.
notes: ZIMSEC; Cambridge Supplement (the branched isomer of C₄H₁₀).

back: A C=C double bond needs at least two carbon atoms; the first alkene is ethene.
